details:
**Tess of the d'Urbervilles** – Hardy’s most famous novel; the tragic heroine Tess is raped by Alec and later marries Angel Clare, making this title a cornerstone clue for the author.

**The Darkling Thrush** – One of Hardy’s best‑known poems, famous for its opening line “I leant upon a coppice gate” and its vivid description of a hopeful bird in a bleak winter landscape.

**The Convergence of the Twain** – Hardy’s elegiac poem about the sinking of the Titanic; it mentions the “Immanent Will” and the “shape of ice” that brought the ships together.

**Far from the Madding Crowd** – A major Hardy novel set in the fictional county of Wessex; it features the love triangle of Gabriel Oak, Bathsheba Everdene, and Frank Troy.

**Jude the Obscure** – Hardy’s controversial novel about the doomed scholar Jude Fawley and his relationships with Sue Bridehead and Arabella Donn; frequently cited in quizbowl.

**Wessex (fictional county)** – The semi‑fictional region of southwest England that serves as the setting for most of Hardy’s novels and poems, often mentioned explicitly in clues.

**Egdon Heath** – The bleak, timeless heathland that forms the backdrop of “The Return of the Native” and several of Hardy’s shorter works; a distinctive geographical clue.

**Angel Clare** – The idealistic young clergyman who marries Tess in “Tess of the d'Urbervilles”; his name recurs in many Hardy‑related questions.

**Alec Stokes (rapist) and his execution at Stonehenge** – Alec rapes Tess and is later murdered by her; the execution scene at Stonehenge is a striking, repeated plot point.

**Little Father Time** – The tragic child in “Jude the Obscure” who, overwhelmed by poverty, kills himself and his siblings; his name appears in multiple clues.

**Sorrow (child’s name)** – The infant daughter born after Tess’s rape, named “Sorrow”; her brief life and death are central to the tragedy of “Tess of the d'Urbervilles”.

**Black flag (signalling execution)** – In “Tess of the d'Urbervilles,” a black flag appears to indicate the impending death of a character, serving as a vivid visual cue.

**Cliffhanger (origin of the term)** – The dramatic scene in “The Return of the Native” where Henry Knight hangs from a cliff, giving rise to the modern phrase “cliffhanger”.

**Stonehenge (site of execution)** – The prehistoric monument where Tess is executed after killing Alec; its use as a setting is a signature Hardy motif.
